sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin and I'm Mark Ronson and welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰，我是马克·朗森，欢迎收听《重构者》，这是一档专注于设计之美及其周边文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl,
sentences.zh: 即使是在我还在夜店打碟的黑胶唱片时代，

sentences.en: every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you and you turned a DJ booth into this like living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 你每晚都要带着 300 件最珍贵的宝贝去工作，把 DJ 台变成一个充满 50 年历史精美文物的流动博物馆。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你最喜欢的播客平台上收听爱彼带来的《重构者》吧。

sentences.en: From the New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is a daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: In 1791, enslaved Haitians did the seemingly impossible, ousting their French masters and founding a nation.
sentences.zh: 1791 年，海地的奴隶们做到了看似不可能的事：他们推翻了法国殖民者，建立了一个国家。

sentences.en: But France made generations of Haitians pay for that freedom in cash.
sentences.zh: 但法国让几代海地人以现金形式偿还了那份自由的代价。

sentences.en: Just how much has remained a mystery until now.
sentences.zh: 直到现在，具体金额仍是一个谜。

sentences.en: Today, my colleague, Catherine Porter, on what a team of Times reporters has found.
sentences.zh: 今天，我的同事凯瑟琳·波特将讲述《时报》记者团队的调查发现。

sentences.en: It's Friday, June 3rd.
sentences.zh: 今天是 6 月 3 日，星期五。

sentences.en: Catherine, just to begin, how and why did this project come to be?
sentences.zh: 凯瑟琳，首先，这个项目是怎么来的，为什么要开展这个项目？

sentences.en: Well,
sentences.zh: 嗯，

sentences.en: I started going to Haiti in 2010 after the earthquake as a journalist for a different paper at that time and was very upset by what I saw because of the death and destruction.
sentences.zh: 2010 年地震后，我作为当时另一家报社的记者开始前往海地，所见所闻的死亡与破坏让我深感不安。

sentences.en: And I kept going back to report on the rebuilding of Haiti.
sentences.zh: 我不断回去报道海地的重建工作。

sentences.en: And over time, I came to see that that destruction, that state of damage was a constant there.
sentences.zh: 随着时间的推移，我逐渐意识到那种破坏和受损的状态在那里是常态。

sentences.en: It wasn't getting better.
sentences.zh: 情况并没有好转。

sentences.en: And at one point, I was doing a story about maternal health.
sentences.zh: 有一次，我在做一个关于孕产妇健康的报道。

sentences.en: And I was in a hospital in Hensh in central Haiti.
sentences.zh: 当时我在海地中部欣什的一家医院里。

sentences.en: And there was a 16-year-old girl on a hospital bed giving birth.
sentences.zh: 病床上有一个 16 岁的女孩正在分娩。

sentences.en: And her baby was lodged sideways.
sentences.zh: 她的胎儿横位卡住了。

sentences.en: And the doctor said to me, like, she's going to die.
sentences.zh: 医生对我说，她快不行了。

sentences.en: We can't get her out because we have no electricity.
sentences.zh: 因为没有电，我们没法给她做手术。

sentences.en: And last time I tried to do an operation, I passed out in the OR because there's no AC.
sentences.zh: 上次我尝试手术时，因为没有空调，我在手术室里晕倒了。

sentences.en: So we can't do it.
sentences.zh: 所以我们做不了。

sentences.en: You know, this is the type of reporting you do when you're in Haiti.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这就是你在海地报道时会遇到的情况。

sentences.en: So you're not only struck by the poverty and the pain, but also the lack of infrastructure is just quite haunting.
sentences.zh: 所以你不仅会被那里的贫困和痛苦所震撼，基础设施的匮乏也同样令人心碎。

sentences.en: While you're there.
sentences.zh: 当你身处那里时。

sentences.en: And, you know, Haiti shares an island.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，海地与另一个国家共享一个岛屿。

sentences.en: The other half of the island is Dominican Republic where they have, like, subsidized health care and education and a functioning subway system.
sentences.zh: 岛的另一半是多米尼加共和国，那里有补贴医疗、教育和运行良好的地铁系统。

sentences.en: And meanwhile, on the other side of the island, they don't have electricity or running water.
sentences.zh: 而与此同时，在岛的另一边，他们连电和自来水都没有。

sentences.en: And it's a resounding question, I think.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一个振聋发聩的问题。

sentences.en: Any foreign correspondent spending time in Haiti has to ask themselves, like, why?
sentences.zh: 任何在海地待过的外国记者都不得不问自己：为什么？

sentences.en: Why is a country like this?
sentences.zh: 为什么一个国家会变成这样？

sentences.en: And the answer you normally get when you ask people about this deeper why is corruption.
sentences.zh: 当你问起人们这个深层原因时，通常得到的答案是腐败。

sentences.en: And we've seen lots of stories of corruption.
sentences.zh: 我们也见过很多关于腐败的报道。

sentences.en: Corruption does play a huge role.
sentences.zh: 腐败确实起到了很大的作用。

sentences.en: But the more I read about Haiti, I started to learn about this thing called the independence debt, which was a series of payments.
sentences.zh: 但随着我对海地了解的深入，我开始接触到一种叫“独立债务”的东西，这是一系列赔款。

sentences.en: The former slaves of Haiti paid to their French colonists for their freedom, for generations, for their independence.
sentences.zh: 海地的前奴隶们为了获得自由，为了独立，向法国殖民者支付了数代的赔款。

sentences.en: Unlike, like, anything I'd ever heard of before or any country had done.
sentences.zh: 这与我以前听说过的任何事情，或者任何国家做过的事情都不同。

sentences.en: And I wanted to learn more and to learn everything I could about it to see what effect it had on the country's trajectory.
sentences.zh: 我想了解更多，尽可能多地了解它，看看它对这个国家的发展轨迹产生了什么影响。

sentences.en: So trying to get to the bottom of how much they paid, who they paid, what was this thing the independence debt?
sentences.zh: 所以，试图弄清楚他们到底付了多少钱，付给了谁，这个“独立债务”到底是什么？

sentences.en: The more we dug into it,
sentences.zh: 我们挖掘得越深，

sentences.en: the more we came to understand that the context of these payments is really critical in understanding the bigger story about why Haiti is as impoverished and underdeveloped as it is today.
sentences.zh: 就越意识到这些赔款的背景对于理解海地为何如此贫困和落后的宏大叙事至关重要。

sentences.en: And so, Catherine, what is the story behind these payments, this independence debt, as it's called?
sentences.zh: 那么，凯瑟琳，这些赔款——也就是所谓的“独立债务”——背后的故事是什么？

sentences.en: What is that history?
sentences.zh: 那段历史是怎样的？

sentences.en: So, to understand the story of the payments, you need to understand the story of colonial Saint-Domingue.
sentences.zh: 要理解赔款的故事，你需要先了解殖民地圣多明各的故事。

sentences.en: So before Haiti was Haiti, it was the most important colony of France.
sentences.zh: 在海地成为海地之前，它是法国最重要的殖民地。

sentences.en: It was a small little nub of an island in the middle of the Caribbean that produced the bulk of sugar and coffee being consumed in all of Europe.
sentences.zh: 它是加勒比海中心一个小小的岛屿，生产了当时整个欧洲消费的大部分糖和咖啡。

sentences.en: It made huge amounts of fortunes for people in France.
sentences.zh: 它为法国人创造了巨额财富。

sentences.en: But it was also considered one of the most brutal places for enslaved people.
sentences.zh: 但它也被认为是奴隶最悲惨的地方之一。

sentences.en: You know, 90% of the population were kidnapped Africans that did not survive very long once they were there.
sentences.zh: 你知道，90% 的人口是被绑架的非洲人，他们到了那里后存活时间并不长。

sentences.en: They didn't reproduce.
sentences.zh: 他们无法繁衍。

sentences.en: They were just simply replaced.
sentences.zh: 他们只是被不断地替换掉。

sentences.en: A couple of years after the French Revolution, there was this revolution started by slaves in Haiti, in which they overthrew their white masters.
sentences.zh: 法国大革命几年后，海地的奴隶发动了革命，推翻了白人统治者。

sentences.en: They set fire to the plantations where they had been subjugated, and the former slaves win.
sentences.zh: 他们烧毁了曾经奴役他们的种植园，前奴隶们赢了。

sentences.en: It's incredible.
sentences.zh: 这太不可思议了。

sentences.en: In 1804, they form the country they call Haiti, and it was the first modern slave rebellion that created the first black republic of the Americas.
sentences.zh: 1804 年，他们建立了名为海地的国家，这是现代第一次奴隶起义，创建了美洲第一个黑人共和国。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: So it's just an amazing story.
sentences.zh: 这真是一个了不起的故事。

sentences.en: So, you know, what happened, though, after is instead of being celebrated, Haiti became a pariah.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，后来发生的事情是，海地不仅没有受到赞美，反而成了被排斥的对象。

sentences.en: So Haiti is free, but totally on its own, very much isolated.
sentences.zh: 海地自由了，但完全孤立无援，非常孤独。

sentences.en: Totally on its own, very much isolated, and completely freaked out, worried that France is going to come back and reconquer.
sentences.zh: 完全孤立无援，非常孤独，而且极度恐慌，担心法国会回来重新征服。

sentences.en: In fact, you know, in 1825, that finally happened.
sentences.zh: 事实上，你知道，1825 年，这种情况最终发生了。

sentences.en: A battalion of warships show up with an emissary of a new king in France, and the emissary is a guy named Baron de Macau, and he says,
sentences.zh: 一支战舰编队带着法国新国王的特使出现了，特使是一个叫麦考男爵的人，他说，

sentences.en: Look, I'm not a negotiator.
sentences.zh: 听着，我不是来谈判的。

sentences.en: You have two choices.
sentences.zh: 你们有两个选择。

sentences.en: Either you pay us reparations for what we've lost, or we declare war.
sentences.zh: 要么支付我们损失的赔偿金，要么我们宣战。

sentences.en: Can you explain that, Kevin, reparations for what we've lost?
sentences.zh: 凯文，你能解释一下吗，“损失的赔偿金”是指什么？

sentences.en: You know, what they had lost was the land and their slaves.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们损失的是土地和奴隶。

sentences.en: So they're talking about both human and physical property.
sentences.zh: 所以他们谈论的是人力和实物财产。

sentences.en: And normally, when we talk about reparations in today's context, it's the opposite.
sentences.zh: 通常，当我们今天谈论赔偿时，情况恰恰相反。

sentences.en: It's reparations for slavery.
sentences.zh: 那是对奴隶制的赔偿。

sentences.en: In this case, it was reparations for lost property.
sentences.zh: 在这种情况下，这是对损失财产的赔偿。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: And how much is France demanding from Haiti?
sentences.zh: 法国向海地索要多少钱？

sentences.en: France is demanding 150 million francs to be paid over five years, which is just impossible, would be impossible for Haiti to pay.
sentences.zh: 法国要求在五年内支付 1.5 亿法郎，这对海地来说是不可能的，根本付不起。

sentences.en: Its budget was just like a small fraction of that.
sentences.zh: 它的预算只是其中的一小部分。

sentences.en: And yet, like, after just three days of talks, the president of Haiti agreed.
sentences.zh: 然而，仅仅经过三天的谈判，海地总统就同意了。

sentences.en: There's still a huge debate among historians as to why.
sentences.zh: 关于原因，历史学家之间仍有巨大的争论。

sentences.en: But for whatever reason, the president at the time agreed that this would be better than going to war.
sentences.zh: 但无论出于什么原因，当时的总统认为这比开战要好。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: So how does Haiti begin to tackle this enormous debt that they have disagreed to?
sentences.zh: 那么海地是如何开始处理这笔他们已经同意的巨额债务的呢？

sentences.en: Well, you know, they couldn't.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你知道，他们根本做不到。

sentences.en: They couldn't even make the first payment.
sentences.zh: 他们连第一笔款项都付不起。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: France knew that Haiti wouldn't be able to pay.
sentences.zh: 法国知道海地付不起。

sentences.en: And so, you know, the French king, the second order he gave to his emissary was not just to get them to sign this deal,
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，法国国王给特使的第二道命令不仅是让他们签下这份协议，

sentences.en: but also to make sure that they took out a loan from a group of young French Parisian banks.
sentences.zh: 还要确保他们从一群年轻的法国巴黎银行那里贷款。

sentences.en: I mean, that's what happened.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，事情就是这样发生的。

sentences.en: They took out a really bad loan from a consortium of French banks to cover the bulk of just the first payment.
sentences.zh: 他们从法国银行财团那里借了一笔非常糟糕的贷款，用来支付第一笔赔款的大部分。

sentences.en: And that is what became known as the double debt.
sentences.zh: 这就是后来所谓的“双重债务”。

sentences.en: And why is it called the double debt?
sentences.zh: 为什么叫“双重债务”？

sentences.en: Well, there's the money that Haiti's paying France and the former French colonists for its independence.
sentences.zh: 嗯，一方面是海地为了独立而向法国和前法国殖民者支付的钱。

sentences.en: And then there's the money it pays back to the banks and the bondholders of that loan.
sentences.zh: 另一方面是它偿还给银行和贷款债券持有人的钱。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And late fees and payments, you know, so essentially there's two debts here.
sentences.zh: 还有滞纳金和利息，所以本质上这里有两笔债务。

sentences.en: That's why it's called the double debt.
sentences.zh: 这就是它被称为双重债务的原因。

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: A debt to France and now a debt to French banks.
sentences.zh: 一笔欠法国的债，现在又多了一笔欠法国银行的债。

sentences.en: So what does Haiti do?
sentences.zh: 那么海地做了什么？

sentences.en: Literally empties its treasury to try and finish that first payment.
sentences.zh: 几乎掏空了国库来试图完成第一笔赔款。

sentences.en: And afterwards it defaults.
sentences.zh: 之后就违约了。

sentences.en: Huh.
sentences.zh: 呵。

sentences.en: And then the Haitian government basically tries everything.
sentences.zh: 然后海地政府基本上尝试了一切办法。

sentences.en: They pass laws for individuals to pay a kind of personal income tax.
sentences.zh: 他们通过法律要求个人缴纳一种个人所得税。

sentences.en: Huh.
sentences.zh: 呵。

sentences.en: Didn't last very long.
sentences.zh: 没持续多久。

sentences.en: They have taxes on stamps.
sentences.zh: 他们对印花税征税。

sentences.en: They try property tax.
sentences.zh: 他们尝试了财产税。

sentences.en: They try a whole bunch of different taxes.
sentences.zh: 他们尝试了各种各样的税收。

sentences.en: But in the end, they end up relying really on one thing.
sentences.zh: 但最终，他们只能依赖一件事。

sentences.en: And that is coffee.
sentences.zh: 那就是咖啡。

sentences.en: Coffee became the number one export in Haiti for more than a century.
sentences.zh: 咖啡在超过一个世纪的时间里成为了海地的第一大出口产品。

sentences.en: They tax coffee exports from coffee farmers that are generally small, subsistence farmers growing coffee trees on small plots of land up in the mountains.
sentences.zh: 他们对咖啡农民征收出口税，这些农民通常是小规模的自给自足农民，在山上的小块土地上种植咖啡树。

sentences.en: So the way Haiti ultimately decides to tackle this debt is to take its most profitable and important product, coffee, tax the heck out of it,
sentences.zh: 所以海地最终决定处理这笔债务的方式是，拿走其最赚钱、最重要的产品——咖啡，对其进行重税，

sentences.en: and ship the bulk of those taxes straight over to France.
sentences.zh: 并将大部分税款直接运往法国。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: You have to remember the thing that's most egregious about the double debt is that Haiti got nothing in return.
sentences.zh: 你必须记住，双重债务最令人愤慨的一点是，海地什么也没得到。

sentences.en: It's not like this was an investment.
sentences.zh: 这不像是一项投资。

sentences.en: Like when we think about debt, you know, international debt today that developing countries take on in order to invest in something like schools or, for that matter, agriculture,
sentences.zh: 就像我们今天考虑债务一样，你知道，发展中国家为了投资学校或农业等领域而承担的国际债务，

sentences.en: which would have been brilliant at the time.
sentences.zh: 那在当时本来会是明智之举。

sentences.en: This money was just simply like a giant drain sucking onto the side of Haiti and going across the ocean to France for nothing in return.
sentences.zh: 但这笔钱就像一个巨大的排水管，吸附在海地身上，跨越海洋流向法国，而海地却一无所获。

sentences.en: But Haiti does make good on these payments.
sentences.zh: 但海地确实履行了这些付款。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: When we were going through the archives, we found that it eventually paid the last part of the double debt in 1888.
sentences.zh: 当我们查阅档案时，发现它最终在 1888 年支付了双重债务的最后一部分。

sentences.en: But, Michael, in order to make those payments, the Haitian government in the 1870s took out two more disastrous loans.
sentences.zh: 但是，迈克尔，为了支付这些款项，海地政府在 19 世纪 70 年代又借了两笔灾难性的贷款。

sentences.en: And so it's kind of like, yeah, they paid their hospital bill, but with their credit card.
sentences.zh: 所以这就像是，是的，他们付清了医院账单，但用的是信用卡。

sentences.en: Like the debt was formally finished, but it continued in another form.
sentences.zh: 债务在形式上结束了，但以另一种形式延续了下来。

sentences.en: And it continued for decades.
sentences.zh: 而且持续了几十年。

sentences.en: And it essentially set Haiti on a course of indebtedness to foreign banks that didn't end until really the late 1950s.
sentences.zh: 它本质上让海地走上了一条对外国银行负债累累的道路，直到 20 世纪 50 年代末才真正结束。

sentences.en: Catherine, at the beginning of this conversation, you said that so much of Haiti's modern woes are tied to these payments.
sentences.zh: 凯瑟琳，在谈话开始时，你说海地现代的许多苦难都与这些赔款有关。

sentences.en: So by the time this double debt is finally paid off, just how much has it cost Haiti?
sentences.zh: 那么，当这笔双重债务最终还清时，它到底让海地付出了多少代价？

sentences.en: So what we found by going through archives and collecting actual payments and tabulating them was that Haiti had paid in total $560 million.
sentences.zh: 我们通过查阅档案、收集实际付款记录并进行汇总，发现海地总共支付了 5.6 亿美元。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Then working with economists, we figured that if that money had just stayed in Haiti, instead of flowing across the ocean to France and just been tucked into people's pockets,
sentences.zh: 然后我们与经济学家合作计算出，如果这笔钱留在海地，而不是流向法国并落入私囊，

sentences.en: it would amount to $21 billion today.
sentences.zh: 按今天的价值计算，相当于 210 亿美元。

sentences.en: A huge sum of money.
sentences.zh: 一笔巨款。

sentences.en: That's the modest end.
sentences.zh: 这还是保守估计。

sentences.en: That's the bottom of the range.
sentences.zh: 这是范围的下限。

sentences.en: Because it's unlikely that that money would have just stayed in people's pockets, right?
sentences.zh: 因为这笔钱不太可能只是留在人们的口袋里，对吧？

sentences.en: They would have used it to send their kids to school, and the government might have used some of it to build roads and bridges, and it would have grown the economy.
sentences.zh: 他们会用它送孩子上学，政府可能会用它修建道路和桥梁，这会促进经济增长。

sentences.en: So in the other scenario, we worked with economists and figured that if the Haitian economy had grown at the same rate as neighboring countries in Latin America,
sentences.zh: 所以在另一种情境下，我们与经济学家合作计算出，如果海地经济能以与拉丁美洲邻国相同的速度增长，

sentences.en: that money would add up to $115 billion today.
sentences.zh: 那笔钱在今天将达到 1150 亿美元。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: So a transformative level of money for a country like Haiti.
sentences.zh: 对于像海地这样的国家来说，这是一笔具有变革意义的资金。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, one to eight times the size of the entire economy today.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，相当于今天整个经济规模的 1 到 8 倍。

sentences.en: So when we think about what France took from Haiti when it demanded that original payment for Haiti's freedom, we should think about it as this much,
sentences.zh: 所以，当我们思考法国在要求海地支付那笔最初的自由赔款时从海地拿走了什么，我们应该想到这个数字，

sentences.en: much bigger number in the billions, which is really, from what you're saying, the economy that Haiti would have had.
sentences.zh: 一个大得多的、以十亿计的数字，这实际上就是你所说的海地本应拥有的经济规模。

sentences.en: If all that money had stayed stayed in the country.
sentences.zh: 如果所有那些钱都留在了国内。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: You know, like, it's really just that opportunity cost that when Haiti was this young country trying to grow and make something of itself, it was hamstrung.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这确实就是一种机会成本，当海地还是一个试图成长并有所作为的年轻国家时，它就受到了束缚。

sentences.en: And we did not have the opportunity to do so.
sentences.zh: 我们没有机会那样做。

sentences.en: We had to look at this as, you know, almost like magical thinking what Haiti might have been had it not been saddled with this huge burden from basically its birth.
sentences.zh: 我们不得不以一种近乎“魔幻思维”的视角来看待这件事：如果海地从诞生之初就没有背负如此沉重的负担，它会是什么样子？

sentences.en: Would Haiti look more like the Dominican Republic now?
sentences.zh: 现在的海地会更像多米尼加共和国吗？

sentences.en: No, like, would there be electricity?
sentences.zh: 不，我是说，会有电力吗？

sentences.en: Would there be more public schools?
sentences.zh: 会有更多的公立学校吗？

sentences.en: Would I have gone to that hospital where that girl was facing death over a difficult pregnancy and found a doctor who had no problem doing an operation on her because the hospital had water and had electricity and had every medication that doctor needed to do it?
sentences.zh: 我会不会去到那家医院，看到那个因妊娠并发症而面临死亡的女孩，并找到一位医生，因为医院有水、有电、有医生所需的一切药物，从而毫无顾虑地为她进行手术？

sentences.en: We don't know what Haiti would look like now.
sentences.zh: 我们不知道现在的海地会是什么样子。

sentences.en: Of course, this is magical thinking.
sentences.zh: 当然，这只是魔幻思维。

sentences.en: But to me, that is the cost that Haiti was forced to pay for this debt that really it should have never have had to pay in the first place.
sentences.zh: 但对我来说，这就是海地被迫为这笔债务付出的代价，而这笔债务它本不该承担。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross-Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 你好，我是安德鲁·罗斯-索金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for DealBook, a daily newsletter at The New York Times.
sentences.zh: 我为《纽约时报》的每日通讯《DealBook》报道商业和政策新闻。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市的DealBook峰会上现场采访一些商业、政治和文化领域最有影响力的领导人，包括J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine Lagarde, Zilran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the DealBook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜·拉加德、齐尔兰·蒙达尼等许多人。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 你可以实时观看其中一些毫无防备、未经剪辑的对话。

sentences.en: We're going to be live streaming select interviews for anyone to watch free at NYTimes.com on November 18th.
sentences.zh: 我们将在11月18日于NYTimes.com上直播部分采访，供所有人免费观看。

sentences.en: If you're not already a subscriber, you can download The New York Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是订阅用户，可以下载《纽约时报》应用程序进行观看，并获得一个月的免费访问权限，阅读我们所有的报道。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 希望你能收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 你一定不想错过。

sentences.en: So, Catherine, we have been focused on the staggering cost of this double debt, this independence debt to Haiti.
sentences.zh: 那么，凯瑟琳，我们一直关注着这笔“双重债务”——即海地的独立债务——所带来的惊人代价。

sentences.en: But, of course, on the other side of this debt was France.
sentences.zh: 但当然，这笔债务的另一端是法国。

sentences.en: So, where did that money go within France, and what impact did it have there?
sentences.zh: 那么，这些钱在法国流向了哪里？又产生了什么影响？

sentences.en: Well, the bulk of that money went to the descendants of former French colonists and slaveholders in France.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这笔钱的大部分流向了法国的前法国殖民者和奴隶主的后裔。

sentences.en: You know, some of whom were still fabulously rich families, you know, merchant families, aristocracy that had invested in Haiti.
sentences.zh: 你知道，其中一些人仍然是极其富有的家族，你知道，那些曾经在海地投资的商人家族、贵族。

sentences.en: We did some genealogy to look at who they are.
sentences.zh: 我们做了一些家谱研究，来看看他们是谁。

sentences.en: In fact, you know, we found the records from a commission that was set up in France to decide how much money each property owner was due.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我们找到了法国设立的一个委员会的记录，该委员会旨在决定每个财产所有者应得多少钱。

sentences.en: And it was amazing to look through the handwritten notes because most of the worth of Saint-Domingue, of the old colony, was in a slave labor.
sentences.zh: 翻阅那些手写笔记真是令人震惊，因为圣多明各（旧殖民地）的大部分财富都建立在奴隶劳动之上。

sentences.en: That land was only producing anything because of the slaves.
sentences.zh: 那片土地之所以能有产出，全靠奴隶。

sentences.en: And they literally calculated the worth of the land based per head of slaves.
sentences.zh: 他们甚至按奴隶人头来计算土地的价值。

sentences.en: So, this is making very clear that these payments are 100% tied to enslaved people in Haiti and what France regards as their value to the ex-slaveholders.
sentences.zh: 所以，这非常清楚地表明，这些赔款与海地的奴隶百分之百挂钩，而法国将其视为前奴隶主应得的价值。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And we found some evidence that there were complaints at the time that this money didn't amount to much because generation after generation,
sentences.zh: 我们还发现了一些证据，显示当时有人抱怨这些钱并没有多少，因为一代又一代地传下去，

sentences.en: it was divvied up between grandchildren and great-grandchildren, more and more and more of them.
sentences.zh: 钱被孙辈、曾孙辈瓜分，人数越来越多。

sentences.en: But many of these families, you know, already had made so much money on the slave trade.
sentences.zh: 但这些家庭中的许多人，你知道，早就在奴隶贸易中赚了大钱。

sentences.en: These were just almost like small dividends long after entering their bank accounts.
sentences.zh: 这些钱在他们进入银行账户很久之后，几乎就像是小额红利一样。

sentences.en: So, this money that, of course,
sentences.zh: 所以，这笔钱，当然，

sentences.en: would have meant so much to the people of Haiti felt like kind of crumbs to these wealthy French families who were getting them generation after generation.
sentences.zh: 本应对海地人民意义重大，但对这些一代又一代领取赔款的富有法国人来说，感觉就像是残羹冷炙。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: It was just like sort of something extra that came in the mail as opposed to something you wait for.
sentences.zh: 这就像是邮寄来的额外收入，而不是你需要苦苦等待的东西。

sentences.en: The other winners on the French side were the French banks.
sentences.zh: 法国方面的另一个赢家是法国银行。

sentences.en: You know, this international loan became a model and Paris became known around the world for international banking.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这种国际贷款成为了一个模式，巴黎也因此在国际银行业界闻名世界。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But I think, like, what this double debt did was exactly what the baron of Macau, that French emissary of the king, hoped it would do.
sentences.zh: 但我认为，这种“双重债务”所做的，正是那位法国国王特使——马考男爵所希望的。

sentences.en: When he left the colony and he wrote his report to the king, he said, under this regime, Haiti would undoubtedly become a highly profitable and costless province of France.
sentences.zh: 当他离开殖民地并向国王提交报告时，他说，在这种体制下，海地无疑将成为法国一个利润丰厚且无需成本的省份。

sentences.en: It was basically a continuing colonization without having to have people on the ground.
sentences.zh: 这基本上是一种无需在当地驻扎人员的持续殖民。

sentences.en: But you could still reap the profits long after the colony had become independent.
sentences.zh: 但你仍然可以在殖民地独立很久之后继续获取利润。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So, the irony is that this arrangement is draining Haiti's economy, to use your word,
sentences.zh: 所以，讽刺的是，这种安排用你的话来说，正在耗尽海地的经济，

sentences.en: and simultaneously kind of seeding the future of the French economy in the form of international banking.
sentences.zh: 同时又以国际银行业的形式为法国经济的未来播下了种子。

sentences.en: And what it so clearly demonstrates is how powerful money on this scale can be in creating institutions, right?
sentences.zh: 这清楚地证明了如此规模的资金在建立机构方面有多么强大，对吧？

sentences.en: And wealth over time, but in this case, not in Haiti, but in France.
sentences.zh: 随着时间的推移创造了财富，但在这种情况下，不是在海地，而是在法国。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: That's really well put, Michael.
sentences.zh: 说得真好，迈克尔。

sentences.en: So, given how upside down all this is,
sentences.zh: 那么，考虑到这一切是多么荒谬，

sentences.en: have there been any meaningful efforts since the establishment of the double debt to get France to pay some or all of this money back to Haiti?
sentences.zh: 自“双重债务”确立以来，是否有过任何有意义的努力，促使法国将这笔钱的部分或全部归还给海地？

sentences.en: Yeah, in 2003, around Haiti's 200th anniversary, a president at the time was a former priest named Jean-Bertrand Aristide.
sentences.zh: 是的，2003年，在海地独立200周年之际，当时的总统是一位前神父，名叫让-贝特朗·阿里斯蒂德。

sentences.en: He launched this campaign for reparations.
sentences.zh: 他发起了这场赔偿运动。

sentences.en: — Demanding for $21 billion in reparations.
sentences.zh: ——要求210亿美元的赔偿。

sentences.en: And it was this remarkable speech in which he's just sort of surprised everyone in the audience, including the French ambassador.
sentences.zh: 那是一场非凡的演讲，他让在场的每个人，包括法国大使，都感到惊讶。

sentences.en: — And that was the beginning.
sentences.zh: ——而那只是开始。

sentences.en: It became this huge campaign with television ads and street banners, you know, rah-rah bans.
sentences.zh: 这演变成了一场声势浩大的运动，有电视广告、街头横幅，你知道，还有各种助威活动。

sentences.en: Even a legal team, international legal team, was putting together elements of a lawsuit.
sentences.zh: 甚至有一个法律团队，一个国际法律团队，正在准备诉讼的要素。

sentences.en: But a year later, before any of this could come to fruition...
sentences.zh: 但一年后，在这一切取得成果之前……

sentences.en: — Rebel forces rolled into Haiti's capital today, a day after President Aristide fled the country.
sentences.zh: ——叛军今天开进了海地首都，就在阿里斯蒂德总统逃离该国的一天后。

sentences.en: — At the same time, several hundred U.S.
sentences.zh: ——与此同时，数百名美国海军陆战队队员，

sentences.en: Marines, along with French troops, began securing key areas in Port-au-Prince.
sentences.zh: 连同法国军队，开始控制太子港的关键区域。

sentences.en: — Aristide was removed from the country by the French and the Americans.
sentences.zh: ——阿里斯蒂德是被法国人和美国人带离该国的。

sentences.en: — By the French and the Americans.
sentences.zh: ——被法国人和美国人。

sentences.en: — Yeah.
sentences.zh: ——是的。

sentences.en: And there's lots of reasons for that.
sentences.zh: 这背后有很多原因。

sentences.en: At the time, the country was roiling with probleMs.
sentences.zh: 当时，这个国家正处于动荡之中。

sentences.en: There was huge opposition to Aristide.
sentences.zh: 阿里斯蒂德面临巨大的反对。

sentences.en: He was facing allegations of human rights abuses, of drug trafficking.
sentences.zh: 他面临着侵犯人权和贩毒的指控。

sentences.en: There was a group of rebels, armed rebels, that were literally bearing down on the capital.
sentences.zh: 有一群叛军，武装叛军，正直接逼近首都。

sentences.en: So on the record, both the French and the Americans said that they were removing him to avoid bloodshed, and it was at his request, or he left willingly.
sentences.zh: 所以官方记录显示，法国和美国都声称他们带走他是为了避免流血，而且是应他的要求，或者他是自愿离开的。

sentences.en: Yet, years later, speaking to former French ambassadors, they say that the demands for reparation, this drumbeat and campaign that Aristide had launched,
sentences.zh: 然而，多年后，在与前法国大使交谈时，他们表示，赔偿要求，即阿里斯蒂德发起的这场声势浩大的运动，

sentences.en: had a part to play, too, that had really rankled the French.
sentences.zh: 也起到了一定作用，这确实激怒了法国人。

sentences.en: They saw it as a trap that risked opening floodgates of demands from all former colonies, and they just wanted to shut it down.
sentences.zh: 他们将其视为一个陷阱，有可能引发所有前殖民地提出赔偿要求，他们只想将其扼杀在摇篮里。

sentences.en: — So France acknowledges that Aristide's demands that France right this historic wrong of the independence debt, it is some factor in the decision to remove him from power.
sentences.zh: ——所以法国承认，阿里斯蒂德要求法国纠正独立债务这一历史错误的诉求，确实是将其赶下台的因素之一。

sentences.en: — Right.
sentences.zh: ——没错。

sentences.en: Like, almost 20 years later, former French ambassador at the time said, yes, this was not the full reason, but it was part of the reason, too.
sentences.zh: 就像近20年后，当时的前法国大使所说，是的，这不是全部原因，但也是原因的一部分。

sentences.en: — Wow.
— And that was the end of the demand for reparations.
sentences.zh: ——而那也是赔偿要求的终结。

sentences.en: It went with him.
sentences.zh: 它随着他的离去而消失了。

sentences.en: — So this very much highlights how much France wants this to be a forgotten chapter of its paSt.
sentences.zh: ——所以这非常突出地表明，法国多么希望这成为其过去被遗忘的一章。

sentences.en: — Right.
sentences.zh: ——没错。

sentences.en: You know, the story of the Haitian Revolution is taught very rarely.
sentences.zh: 你知道，海地革命的故事很少被教授。

sentences.en: Only 10% of French schools teach anything about the Haitian Revolution.
sentences.zh: 只有10%的法国学校教授有关海地革命的内容。

sentences.en: And the story about the double debt, like, that is not on the French curriculum at any level.
sentences.zh: 而关于“双重债务”的故事，在法国的任何课程中都没有出现。

sentences.en: — Interesting.
sentences.zh: ——有意思。

sentences.en: — This is history that France has worked to ignore, to smother, to silence, because it's expensive and it's painful.
sentences.zh: ——这是法国一直试图忽视、掩盖、噤声的历史，因为它代价高昂且令人痛苦。

sentences.en: — But of course, Catherine, because of this project that you and our colleagues undertook, this subject is being discussed very widely at this very moment.
sentences.zh: ——但当然，凯瑟琳，因为你和我们的同事所做的这个项目，这个话题此刻正在被广泛讨论。

sentences.en: So when the Times published everything that you and our colleagues found about this double debt, what was the response inside France?
sentences.zh: 那么，当《时报》发表了你和同事们关于这笔“双重债务”的所有发现时，法国国内有什么反应？

sentences.en: — Well, this has stirred a lot of media coverage in France.
sentences.zh: ——嗯，这在法国引起了大量的媒体报道。

sentences.en: There are columnists writing about it, radio shows talking about it.
sentences.zh: 有专栏作家在写相关文章，广播节目也在讨论它。

sentences.en: One of the French banks we highlighted that was very involved in later years, it now goes by the name Credit Mutuelle, and put out a statement that it was horrified,
sentences.zh: 我们重点提到的其中一家在后期深度参与的法国银行，现在改名为法国互助信贷银行（Credit Mutuelle），它发表声明称感到震惊，

sentences.en: and that it was hiring a team of scholars, including Haitian researchers, to bring the full history to light.
sentences.zh: 并表示将聘请一个学者团队，包括海地研究人员，来揭示全部历史。

sentences.en: But from the French government, there's been nothing but silence.
sentences.zh: 但法国政府方面，除了沉默还是沉默。

sentences.en: — Total silence.
sentences.zh: ——彻底的沉默。

sentences.en: — We have not had a reaction whatsoever from them.
sentences.zh: ——我们没有收到他们任何形式的反应。

sentences.en: — So it does not seem like the possibility of France paying reparations has really changed here.
sentences.zh: ——所以看起来法国支付赔偿的可能性并没有真正改变。

sentences.en: That possibility still seems very small.
sentences.zh: 这种可能性看起来仍然非常渺茫。

sentences.en: — Yeah, I see no indication that that has changed.
sentences.zh: ——是的，我没看到任何迹象表明情况有所改变。

sentences.en: — And what about the reaction in Haiti?
sentences.zh: ——那海地的反应如何？

sentences.en: — The reaction has been huge.
sentences.zh: ——反应非常强烈。

sentences.en: — The Haitian media has really been running with this story.
sentences.zh: ——海地媒体确实一直在报道这个故事。

sentences.en: — It's been filling the airwaves of the radio, on TV.
sentences.zh: 它充斥着广播和电视的频道。

sentences.en: Talk show hosts have been talking about it.
sentences.zh: 脱口秀主持人在讨论它。

sentences.en: The newspaper has been printing parts of the story.
sentences.zh: 报纸也在刊登故事的部分内容。

sentences.en: — Wow.
— But the most amazing reaction to me has been the emotional reaction among both Haitians in Haiti and the Haitian diaspora, particularly in the United States.
sentences.zh: ——但对我来说，最令人惊叹的反应是海地国内的海地人以及海地侨民，特别是美国海地侨民的情感反应。

sentences.en: You know, one Haitian American told me that she felt like she was a person who had suffered abuse for years, and that the series kind of was an acknowledgment of the abuse,
sentences.zh: 你知道，一位海地裔美国人告诉我，她感觉自己像是一个多年来遭受虐待的人，而这个系列报道是对这种虐待的一种承认，

sentences.en: and that up until now, it was almost like this history that had been so silenced that you'd feel like you're stupid or insane to think it.
sentences.zh: 而且直到现在，这段历史几乎被噤声，以至于如果你去想它，你会觉得自己很愚蠢或疯了。

sentences.en: — And that it had really been Haitians themselves had been blamed for their own lack of development.
sentences.zh: ——而且海地人自己一直被指责为自身发展不足。

sentences.en: And this was kind of like a vindication that the story that they knew to be true and they had told themselves was recognized by outsiders.
sentences.zh: 这就像是一种平反，他们所知道的真实故事以及他们对自己讲述的故事，得到了外界的认可。

sentences.en: — Mm-hmm.
I'm curious, Catherine, how you think about the value of this project.
sentences.zh: 我很好奇，凯瑟琳，你是如何看待这个项目的价值的？

sentences.en: I mean, if it's not going to result in France repaying this vast sum of money to Haiti,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，如果它不能导致法国向海地偿还这笔巨款，

sentences.en: if it's not going to allow Haiti to reclaim this $115 billion in economic activity that it was deprived of, what is the value of having determined the cost of this to Haiti?
sentences.zh: 如果它不能让海地收回被剥夺的1150亿美元经济活动，那么确定海地所付出的代价有什么价值呢？

sentences.en: — Now, I interviewed this really interesting PhD history student who's studying Saint-Domingue, the colony of Haiti before it was Haiti.
sentences.zh: ——我采访了一位非常有意思的博士历史系学生，他正在研究圣多明各，即海地成为海地之前的殖民地。

sentences.en: And he told me he thought about the double debt every week.
sentences.zh: 他告诉我他每周都会想到“双重债务”。

sentences.en: And I asked him, like, why?
sentences.zh: 我问他，为什么？

sentences.en: Because he was studying colonial Haiti, like Saint-Domingue, before it became independent.
sentences.zh: 因为他研究的是殖民时期的海地，也就是独立前的圣多明各。

sentences.en: And, you know, his response has really stuck with me.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他的回答真的让我印象深刻。

sentences.en: He said he thought it was just so unfair that France has this motto, and it's known around the world for it, of being the country of liberty, of fraternity, of equality.
sentences.zh: 他说他觉得法国拥有这样一个座右铭非常不公平，而且它因此闻名于世，即“自由、博爱、平等”。

sentences.en: Like, that's its theme.
sentences.zh: 就像，那是它的主题。

sentences.en: But Haiti is known for corruption, for poverty, for despair.
sentences.zh: 但海地却以腐败、贫困和绝望而闻名。

sentences.en: — Right.
sentences.zh: ——没错。

sentences.en: — You know, and this year we spent looking deeply at this really calls both of those things into question.
sentences.zh: ——你知道，我们花了一年时间深入研究，这确实对这两者都提出了质疑。

sentences.en: Like, when it comes to Haiti, I do not think France's tagline has been liberty, fraternity, or equality.
sentences.zh: 比如，当谈到海地时，我不认为法国的口号是自由、博爱或平等。

sentences.en: — Quite the opposite.
sentences.zh: ——恰恰相反。

sentences.en: — Quite the opposite.
sentences.zh: ——恰恰相反。

sentences.en: You know, and when you look at the history of Haiti, among the taglines we should be including is that this was the first place in the Americas
sentences.zh: 你知道，当你审视海地的历史时，我们应该加入的口号之一是：这是美洲第一个

sentences.en: that threw off slavery and declared Black people free.
sentences.zh: 摆脱奴隶制并宣布黑人自由的地方。

sentences.en: And it was made to pay for that for generations.
sentences.zh: 而它却被迫为此付出了几代人的代价。

sentences.en: — Well, Catherine, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: ——好的，凯瑟琳，非常感谢你。

sentences.en: We appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 我们很感激。

sentences.en: — And thanks for having me on, Michael.
sentences.zh: ——也谢谢你邀请我来，迈克尔。

sentences.en: — We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: ——我们马上回来。

sentences.en: — The New York Times app?
sentences.zh: ——《纽约时报》应用程序？

sentences.en: Unlocked?
sentences.zh: 解锁了？

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to the Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 每个人都知道你需要订阅《时报》才能访问所有的报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore the Times for a month, for free, without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但如果你可以免费试用《时报》一个月，且无需输入信用卡信息呢？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在你可以了。

sentences.en: When you download the New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 当你第一次下载《纽约时报》应用程序时，你在应用中的第一个月是免费的。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 用一个月的时间越过付费墙，看看《时报》订阅者每天都能获得什么。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to the New York Times, download the Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果你还没有订阅《纽约时报》，今天就下载《时报》应用程序，获得30天的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是您今天还需要了解的其他新闻。

sentences.en: — After Columbine, after Sandy Hook, after Charleston, after Orlando, after Las Vegas, after Parkland, nothing has been done.
sentences.zh: ——在科伦拜恩、桑迪胡克、查尔斯顿、奥兰多、拉斯维加斯和帕克兰枪击案之后，什么都没有改变。

sentences.en: — In a speech on Thursday, President Biden said that a series of deadly mass shootings in New York, Texas, and Oklahoma required Congress to end years of inaction
sentences.zh: ——拜登总统在周四的演讲中表示，纽约、德克萨斯和俄克拉荷马州发生的一系列致命大规模枪击事件，要求国会结束多年来的不作为，

sentences.en: by passing new federal gun safety laws.
sentences.zh: 通过新的联邦枪支安全法。

sentences.en: — This time that can't be true.
sentences.zh: ——这一次不能再这样了。

sentences.en: This time we must actually do something.
sentences.zh: 这一次我们必须真正采取行动。

sentences.en: The president called for a ban on assault weapons and high-capacity magazines, the expansion of background checks for gun buyers, and the adoption of red flag laws.
sentences.zh: 总统呼吁禁止攻击性武器和大容量弹匣，扩大对购枪者的背景调查，并采纳“红旗法”。

sentences.en: But few, if any, of those proposals are likely to overcome opposition from congressional Republicans, a reality that Biden angrily acknowledged.
sentences.zh: 但这些提议几乎不可能克服国会共和党人的反对，拜登愤怒地承认了这一现实。

sentences.en: But my God, the fact that the majority of the Senate Republicans don't want any of these proposals even to be debated or come up for a vote, I find unconscionable.
sentences.zh: 但天哪，大多数参议院共和党人甚至不想让这些提议进入辩论或投票环节，我觉得这简直不可理喻。

sentences.en: We can't fail the American people again.
sentences.zh: 我们不能再次辜负美国人民。

sentences.en: — Today's episode was produced by Muj Zady, Rob Zipko, Will Reed, and Eric Krupke.
sentences.zh: ——今天的节目由Muj Zady、Rob Zipko、Will Reed和Eric Krupke制作。

sentences.en: It was edited by M.J.
sentences.zh: 由M.J.编辑，

sentences.en: Davis Lynn and Patricia Willens, contains original music by Marian Lozano and Rowan Nimisto, and was engineered by Dan Powell.
sentences.zh: Davis Lynn和Patricia Willens参与，包含Marian Lozano和Rowan Nimisto的原创音乐，由Dan Powell负责工程制作。

sentences.en: — Our theme music is by Jim Brunberg and Ben Landferk of Winderly.
sentences.zh: ——我们的主题音乐由Winderly的Jim Brunberg和Ben Landferk创作。

sentences.en: Special thanks to Constant Mea, Matt Apuzo, Salam Gubrekidon, and Harold Isaac.
sentences.zh: 特别感谢Constant Mea、Matt Apuzo、Salam Gubrekidon和Harold Isaac。

sentences.en: — That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: ——以上就是本期《每日新闻》的全部内容。

sentences.en: I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: See you on Monday.
sentences.zh: 周一见。

sentences.en: — This week on The Wirecutter Show, we're getting ready for hosting over the holidays.
sentences.zh: ——本周的《Wirecutter秀》将为您准备节日待客指南。

sentences.en: Tune in for tips on making your guests feel at home.
sentences.zh: 敬请收听，获取让客人宾至如归的小贴士。

sentences.en: — Are they a blackout sleeper?
sentences.zh: ——他们是那种需要全黑环境才能入睡的人吗？

sentences.en: I don't mean do they blackout to go to sleep.
sentences.zh: 我不是指他们是不是喝到断片才睡着。

sentences.en: I mean, what kind of light do they require?
sentences.zh: 我是说，他们对光线有什么要求？

sentences.en: Because that is a very specific thing.
sentences.zh: 因为这非常讲究。

sentences.en: Do they have allergies, food sensitivities?
sentences.zh: 他们有过敏或食物不耐受吗？

sentences.en: Are they coffee tea drinkers?
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢喝咖啡还是茶？

sentences.en: What time do they like to get up?
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢几点起床？

sentences.en: — Find The Wirecutter Show on The New York Times app or wherever you like to listen.
sentences.zh: ——您可以在《纽约时报》App或您喜欢的任何播客平台收听《Wirecutter秀》。
